briefTitle: Phase III Study of Datopotamab Deruxtecan Versus Docetaxel in Previously Treated TROP2-positive Advanced or Metastatic Non-squamous NSCLC Without Actionable Genomic Alterations

typedChecks.sourceText: Pathologically documented Stage IIIB, IIIC, or Stage IV non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Has no known tumour genomic alterations in NTRK, BRAF V600, RET, MET exon 14 skipping, KRAS G12C, or HER2. Additionally, participants must not have known tumour genomic alteration of any other actionable driver oncogenes for which there are locally approved targeted first-line therapies.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Multiple specific and general negative mutation criteria spanning multiple genes without single typed kinds for all mentioned targets.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Prospectively assessed TROP2 NMR positive based on results from an appropriately validated investigational TROP2 RxDx device
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: TROP2 biomarker status is not among the allowed typed kinds.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participants must have received platinum based chemotherapy (PBC) in combination with anti-programmed death-protein 1 (anti-PD-1)/anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (anti-PD-L1) monoclonal antibody (mAb) as the only prior line of therapy or received PBC and anti-PD-1/anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody (in either order) sequentially as the only 2 prior lines of therapy.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Complex prior line therapy combination rules cannot be expressed as a simple typed prior_lines or prior_therapy check.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: At least one lesion not previously irradiated that qualifies as a Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, Version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1) target lesion
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Measurable disease by RECIST is a subjective imaging judgment, not a typed kind.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Squamous, mixed NSCLC, or small cell lung cancer (SCLC) histology.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Exclusion of mixed histology and small cell lung cancer cannot be fully captured by typed histology rules.
